title: A 50-Year-Old Frog Mystery Points to a Fungus
paragraphs: In the 1970s, many frogs lived in the Atlantic Forest in Brazil. Then, in the early 1980s, many of them disappeared. For about fifty years, nobody knew the reason.

A team from the Smithsonian and Penn State tested hundreds of old frogs kept in a museum. The frogs came from one place in São Paulo and from seventeen different species. The team looked for a fungus called chytrid, which can make frogs very sick.

None of the frogs from before 1979 had the fungus. More than half of the frogs from the 1980s had it. Between 2022 and 2024, scientists visited the forest again and found twelve of the seventeen species. The fungus is still there, but most frogs seem to be doing better now.

questions.q: What did the team look for in the old frogs?
How many species did they find again in 2022–2024?
Did frogs from before 1979 have the fungus?
